[spoiler=[b]The Sand Cat[/b] (Nordeheim)]

The gravel of the site crunched under his boots, the desert sun baking the ground not given the safety of shade. First the country goes insane, now he has to learn to command an entirely separate vehicle than he is used to. Least the beach gives some comfort for him and his men before they get shipped out to the front after training. Reaching the shade of the temporary storage area, the corrugated metal roof gives a break from the direct sunlight. After taking a few moments to take a sip from his canteen, he finds his crew familiarizing themselves with the tank, making general inspections, as well as trying to cope with the heat.

The man to take notice of Lieutenant Jabril would be their gunner, Musab. What do you think, commander? The man smiles a big goofy grin, patting the tank as he hangs out one of the turrets side hatches. 

Jabril takes a bit to look over the tank before responding. He knows the vehicle well, after all its extensive use by Nordeheim during their Noble War makes it a battle proven vehicle. The long 75mm main cannon provides substantial power against soft targets and other tanks, and the armor can deflect some shots. Only issue is it has never been proven in desert combat, meaning his men are riding on something that could fall to an unforeseen engineering oversight. 

Where is our driver? Jabril would ask, taking a walk around the tank to do a light visual inspection. 

That kid? No idea. Might as well be staring into the sun for all I know. 

Wow, very insightful my friend, the commander would quip back sarcastically, giving his gunner a light punch in the side. Who did the paint job? I know it wasnt you, ive seen your drawings you make during briefings

Hey! That hurts you know. But anyhow, apparently some guy in the other unit here getting familiarized with equipment is an avid painter. Gave him some of the nice tea rations for it.

Nodding his head, Jabril would raise another question. And where did you get those? 

Musab smiled again, only offering a slight shrug as an answer. 

How many times do I have to remind you that just because youre friends with the mess officer doesnt mean you can just take from there? 

Hey! I didnt get them from there! This time at least

After letting out a long sigh, Jabril would shake his head. Just where are the others?

Oh, they are in the recreational center. Not much to do out here as it seems like all we need are some sand filters, plus the rec center has air conditioning, the tank doesnt.

You have a point.

As they walk to the building, two tankers stop to look towards the railyard where yet more tanks are being unloaded.

Did you see those tanks those expeditionary forces were unloading at port when we were on leave? Jabril asks, adjusting his hat so as to block the sun better.

Yah, the weird looking ones? I wonder why they even brought them.

They are heavy tanks apparently. Wont have a fun time the second they get out of that city they are keeping them in.

Might as well give them some ditches and make them bunkers, huh?

Yep say, when do you think the command will move us out?

Musab would scoff and roll his eyes. You of anyone should know that the coalition command is the most unorganized thing on the planet. I bet they will panic and rush us to the front the second those communists start pushing against us instead of the small battles that have been happening.

Let's hope that they can focus on commanding instead of arguing amongst each other. Would be a miracle though.[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Overview of the war[/b] (Informational)]

The current climate of Sabrata is tense and fragmented, but the main fighting is yet to come. Battlelines are being established, trenches dug and units mobilized. Small battles break out along the lines of coalition and revolutionary control, however the land between the royalists and revolutionaries remains in erie silence. A storm is brewing in the east, one that will soon push west and rain fire and death upon those who stand in its way. Increasing numbers of citizens from all sides make the journey to the borders of neighboring countries to escape the conflict.

Talks between the coalition and royalists have started, but it will be a while before they can see eye to eye, much less work together. As the delegation from Hydronia travel, supplies and units from Nordiheim have already made landfall in the west. The city of Stikada now sees the sole Lavian base in the borders of Sabrata begin major fortification efforts, establishing a much larger airfield than the current city has as well as offering weapons training to those who want it. All of Sabrata stands waiting as factories from its once flourishing industrial sector now push out munitions and guns. No matter what Sabrata is in the eyes of the nations who are involved, its fields will soon be flooded with the blood of soldiers.[/spoiler]

II needdd to go to the restroom.
Ironvisak pushed himself up from the chair, ears ringing from the gunfire, blood dripping down the front of his uniform. His vision shook. The world felt distant.

He stumbled down the marble hallway, each step echoing behind him as he left the chaos and screams inside the hall. The shrill whistle in his ears mixed with the pounding of his pulse, turning every heartbeat into a muffled explosion.

At the building entrance, two DESF guards stood rigid, armor cracked, visors up, smoke curling from their cigarettes. They straightened the moment they saw him approach, waiting for an order they feared might come.

Ironvisak didnt speak.
Didnt even look at them.

He pushed through the side door into the courtyard.

The cold night air slammed into him like a wall.

No cameras.
No journalists.
No advisors.
Only the pale glow of the courtyard lamps and the wailing of distant sirens as ambulances rushed toward the hall.

Ironvisak drew in a shaky breath and reached into his coat.

He pulled out the government-issued XED-089 iPhone  elite, encrypted, and reserved only for senior officials.

He scrolled past every contact. until he reached a single number.

+77  991*

His thumb hovered.

His breath steamed in the cold.

Thenhe pressed CALL.

One ring.
Two rings.

On the third:

Click.

Absolute silence.

Then a distorted voice, calm almost gentle:

You were warned this would happen.

Ironvisaks jaw tightened.
Through the courtyard glass he saw medics sprinting, President Achebe shouting orders, and Dr. Helenas screams tearing through the hall.

I didnt order the shooting, Ironvisak growled. Protocol 4 was activated remotely. Someone accessed my override codes.

A quiet, knowing laugh seeped through the receiver.

You still believe those codes belong to you?

His stomach twisted.

Listen, Ironvisak snapped. That kid called me Gerichmen. That name hasnt existed in decades. No one alive should

Mistakes were made.
The voice cut him off.
Loose ends survived. Today, one of them spoke.

Ironvisaks breath hitched.

So it was you, he whispered.

No, the voice replied.
It was you.

Ironvisak froze.
The night air suddenly felt suffocating.

What the hell is that supposed to mean?

A long, cold pause.

Then the voice spoke with chilling certainty:

You dont remember what happened in the Night Eircks Program. But others do.

Ironvisak staggered back a step.

Y-yeah? What about it? he muttered, fear creeping into his voice.

The voice sharpened.

Night Eircks links to you, Gerichmen. You forget that Herman gave you the order himself. You were supposed to take care of the problem.

Ironvisak exploded:

LISTEN! HERMAN WAS NOT IN THE RIGHT MIND! YOU KNOW DAMN WELL HE WANTED TO WIPE THEM OUT! I didnt!

Silence.

Then, almost soothingly:

Okay, President Willham. Believe what you want. Today was only the beginning. And if you do not control the story the story will consume you.

Ironvisak felt his hand tremble.

What about Kal? he whispered. The boy he

The voice answered without emotion.

One fewer witness.

Something in Ironvisak snapped.

With a furious shout, he slammed the phone against the stone wall.
The device cracked, sparked and shattered in his grip.

The line went dead.

Footsteps pounded behind him.

Mr. President! an aide gasped, breathless. Theyre asking for you. President Achebe is furious. Cameras are rolling already. They need a statement immediately!

Ironvisak wiped the blood from his cheek.
Straightened his torn uniform.
Set his jaw.

Tell them, he said quietly, his voice echoing in the cold air,
that the United States of Oceancice will cooperate in a full investigation.

The aide nodded and ran back inside.
